questions.question: List three treatments for head lice (pediculosis capitis).

parts.text: Name three treatments for head lice.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) 1%–5% permethrin cream rinse (Nix/Acticin), applied topically with a second application 7–10 days later. (2) 0.33% pyrethrins plus 4% piperonyl butoxide shampoo (RID/A-200), 95% ovicidal, repeated in 7–10 days. (3) Ivermectin — either topical 0.5% ivermectin lotion (Sklice, single 10-min application) or oral ivermectin 200–400 µg/kg repeated at 7–10 days — which kills nymphs as they emerge and is useful for pyrethroid-resistant lice. (Other accepted options from Table 292.1: 0.5% malathion lotion, 0.9% spinosad suspension, 5% benzyl alcohol lotion.) All regimens require two treatments 7–10 days apart plus wet-combing to remove viable nits.

cohort_answer.text: CPS statement: Pyrethrin, piperonyl butoxide (shampoo and conditioner); Permethrin 1%; 50% isopropyl myristate and 50% ST-cyclomethicone; Dimethicone solution. All need retreatment in 7 days.
